html:
SMTO-LLM-0065 — This model server would be reachable from other computers

GUID: 383d1d1c-767f-5481-ac95-aa26878019b0
Slug: local-ai-external-bind-requires-confirmation
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • Your profile sets the model server to accept connections from other computers. SMTO won't do that until it's approved and protected with a key, so nothing was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If only that computer needs the model server, open the profile in Parameter Store, set host to 127.0.0.1, and select Save. 127.0.0.1 keeps the server private to that computer, so no extra approval is needed.
  2. If other computers need it, create a Local AI API key parameter, put its reference in api_key_ref, set external_bind_confirmed to true, and save. A key stops strangers on the network from using your model server.
  3. Also ask the person who manages that Gateway to allow outside access to model servers on it. The Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses on that computer, must agree as well.
  4. Then start the model server again in a new message that names both the profile and its key with @. Nothing was started this time, and SMTO only uses the profile and key you name in the message.

What success looks like

  • The model server starts and its status shows ready at the address you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't open the model server to other computers without a key and a trusted network.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The profile binds to a non-loopback or wildcard host, and the start lacked external_bind_confirmed in the profile, GATEWAY_LOCAL_AI_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_BIND on the Gateway, or an API key via api_key_ref, so no process was created.

What this means

  • Non-loopback launch requires profile confirmation, Gateway operator opt-in and a supplied key before process creation. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • Non-loopback launch requires profile confirmation, Gateway operator opt-in and a supplied key before process creation.

How to diagnose it

  • Check profile exposure confirmation, Gateway external-bind policy and credential availability separately; assess which provider endpoints the key actually protects.

How to fix it

  • If remote access isn't needed, set host to 127.0.0.1. Otherwise set external_bind_confirmed true, store a key with the Local AI API key template, reference it in api_key_ref and accept both Parameter references in the task, and have the Gateway operator set GATEWAY_LOCAL_AI_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_BIND=true and restart the Gateway. Managed Ollama rejects a key, so it cannot be bound externally through SMTO. These checks don't add a firewall or TLS, so keep the endpoint behind a trusted network or reverse proxy.
  • Use loopback when remote exposure is unnecessary; otherwise have the operator explicitly configure the supported authentication and network boundary.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • All exposure prerequisites are satisfied and the operator has verified the intended network boundary.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
